summary: All-optical initialization, coherent control, and single-shot readout of $^{167}$Er nuclear spin qubits are demonstrated by embedding dopants in yttrium orthosilicate within a 65 MHz linewidth Fabry-Perot cavity that selectively enhances spin-preserving transitions. A large 6.8 T magnetic field freezes paramagnetic impurities, enabling 91(2)% readout fidelity, $T_2^* = 0.62(3)$ ms dephasing time, and coherence times reaching 0.28(8) s under dynamical decoupling, establishing a promising platform for fiber-based quantum networks at telecommunications wavelengths.
motivation: Nuclear spins offer exceptional coherence for quantum memories in repeaters and networks, but direct all-optical control and readout of individual nuclear spin qubits in solids has been outstanding. The combination of long storage times, minimal fiber loss in the C-band, and frequency-multiplexed addressing motivates using $^{167}$Er:YSO as a quantum networking platform.
method: A 10.9 µm YSO membrane containing $^{167}$Er dopants is integrated into a frequency-tunable Fabry-Perot cavity (Q = 3 × 10$^6$, linewidth 65 MHz) operated at <1.8 K in 6.8 T magnetic field. Optical pumping on $\Delta m_I = -1$ red-sideband transitions initializes the qubit, selective cavity enhancement of $\Delta m_I = 0$ spin-preserving transitions (Purcell factor up to 95) enables single-shot readout, and two-photon Raman transitions with 90 MHz detuning provide coherent control while suppressing scattering.
result: Single-shot readout fidelity reaches 91(2)% (limited by 43.9 Hz dark counts; >98% expected with better detectors), $T_2^\text{Hahn} = 16.7(9)$ ms in Hahn-echo, and $T_\text{DD} = 0.28(8)$ s with 64-pulse XY decoupling scaling as $N^{0.82(2)}$, while T$_1$ exceeds 33 s at 1.72 K and spin lifetime $T_1 > 0.2$ s is achieved at applied field.
